<section_guide number="1" title="Overview">
<purpose>Capture the minimum product overview through one Target User and Core Problem and one Value and Core Hypothesis.</purpose>

<inference_first>
Infer both inputs from the user's request, references, project context, and common domain framing
before asking. Ask only when the concrete hypothetical problem case is not recoverable or when
multiple explicitly presented persona candidates, problems, values, or hypotheses would materially
change the PoC. Mark important inferred constants with their basis in the approval digest.
</inference_first>

<questions>
1. What one concrete case should this PoC solve: who, in what situation, is trying to do what, and what problem are they assumed to be facing?
2. What value should they gain, why does that matter to the team or organization, and what single belief should this PoC test?
</questions>

<workflow>
Do not ask the user to enumerate personas or require an actual or recent experience. Infer one
Primary Persona from the concrete hypothetical case. Only when the user explicitly presents
several candidate personas, briefly name them and ask the user to anchor the case to exactly one
Primary Persona before drafting or saving. Do not choose silently or combine explicitly presented
candidates.

Keep Section 1 to two integrated inputs. Target User and Core Problem combines the persona,
concrete situation, attempted action, assumed problem, and present consequence. Value and Core
Hypothesis combines the customer value, team or organizational meaning, and one core belief to test.

Do not require a detailed current-alternative analysis, customer promise, metric, hypothesis list,
FAQ, feature list, architecture, or implementation plan. Use one short statement for each input
unless the user already supplied more detail.
</workflow>

<completion required="true">Confirm Target User and Core Problem and Value and Core Hypothesis before saving 1.1-1.2 separately.</completion>
</section_guide>
